blocking_findings: P1 BFCACHE-RESTORE: assets/scene.js:181-185,187-191,205-208 permanently dispose on pagehide, including persisted=true, with no pageshow restore. Reproduced native Back navigation from /index.htm?judge-away=1 to /: pagehide/pageshow both persisted=true and the document marker survives, but frames remain 131, renderer becomes static and ScrollTriggers fall from 5 to 0. Clicking pause changes paused=true while aria-pressed remains false, the label stays Pause motion, and root stays motion-on; switching BG leaves that English label. Narrow fix: reversible persisted-page suspension/resumption, or a pageshow reinitializer that resets disposed/renderer/context/scrollFrame, reconnects observers, recomputes inView and active chapter, restores current preferences and rebuilds choreography without replaying entrance. Add a real BFCache regression test for motion, pause/CSS transitions, language and reduced-motion state.

P1 DESKTOP-ART-ACCESSIBILITY: assets/styles.css:8 (.js .topic-art{display:none}), assets/scene.js:24-28 and index.html:89 hide both accessible versions of the six chapter artworks: semantic originals are display:none, while visible stage clones have empty alt inside aria-hidden=true. Chromium Accessibility.getFullAXTree exposes only hero and closing images at 1440px, versus all eight image descriptions at 390px. This removes the six meaningful bilingual scene descriptions from desktop assistive-technology reading, contrary to the semantic-source contract. Narrow fix: visually hide, rather than display:none, the semantic chapter figures on enhanced desktop while preserving their accessibility-tree presence and document order; keep the duplicate stage decorative. Verify all eight localized image names in EN/BG at both breakpoints without duplicate announcements.
nonblocking_findings: Documentation drift: PRODUCT.md still specifies Daylight Glasshouse, Onest and locally authored 3D originals; the surface brief still says implementation/browser verification pending. DESIGN.md and the handoff correctly describe the current pinned sanctuary and GPT-produced sources. Reconcile obsolete product/surface statements without rerolling or changing the design.

Shader portability risk: assets/scene.js:110 calls smoothstep(1.,.78,uv.y), whose reversed edges are undefined by GLSL ES. No resulting corruption was observed in this Chromium software-WebGL run. Prefer 1.0-smoothstep(.78,1.0,uv.y) to express the intended inverse ramp portably.

Evidence limits are correctly disclosed, not release blockers: four builder axe runs contain zero A/AA violations but retain incomplete image-backed contrast checks; no full accessibility certification follows. Background-tab frame freezing is not native document.hidden observation; the visibility handler was separately tested with a synthetic flag. The 12.04-second MP4 is a timed capture sequence, not a continuous high-frame-rate recording or field-performance proof.
summary: FAIL: two independently reproduced release blockers remain: BFCache return permanently breaks motion lifecycle/control synchronization, and enhanced desktop removes six semantic artwork descriptions from the accessibility tree. The pinned visual direction, eight-original asset pipeline, ordinary motion/fallback behavior and unchanged hardened server otherwise have substantial supporting evidence. No deployment or production verification was performed.
